title: Aamir Khan Is Getting Married at Home, in His Living Room, With No Cameras. And the Whole Country Can't Look Away.
excerpt: On July 5, the most calculated star in Bollywood will quietly marry Bengaluru wellness entrepreneur Gauri Spratt in a registered ceremony — no destination palace, no drone shots, just two families and a superstar who insists he doesn't get the fuss.
body:
Three weddings. Two divorces, both amicable. One superstar who insists he doesn't understand the fuss — even as the entire country leans in to watch. On **July 5**, **Aamir Khan**, the most cerebral of the Khans, will quietly marry **Gauri Spratt** at home in Mumbai, and the contrast between the size of the ceremony and the size of the curiosity tells you everything about where Bollywood is in 2026.

No destination palace. No drone footage. No 400-guest sangeet leaking to Instagram before the mehendi dries. Just a registered marriage in his living room, two families, and a handful of people who actually matter to him.

> "It will be very private. It's a very simple registered marriage, at home, with just both families and really close friends. We both want to keep it very basic." — Aamir Khan, to Variety India

For a man whose last on-screen romance involved running through wheat fields, this is almost defiantly unromantic in its staging — and that's precisely the point. Aamir has spent the last year talking about Gauri the way people talk about coming home, not the way stars usually talk about a third act. At 61, he isn't selling a fairy tale. He's quietly closing one.


![Variety India — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/5/5a/Variety_cover.jpg)



> **"Veteran actress **Rakhee Gulzar** had earlier defended his decision to marry again at 60, calling him "a very sincere person." When the old guard is this protective, you know the affection is real."**



**Who is Gauri Spratt?** Not a name the paparazzi knew until Aamir made it one. Based in Bengaluru, she works in the wellness and beauty space, lives largely off the grid — her Instagram has all of sixteen posts — and carries an unexpectedly literary lineage: she's the granddaughter of **Philip Spratt**, the British-born writer and thinker who came to India in the 1920s and never left. She has a son, Quinn, from a previous marriage. She is, in other words, exactly the kind of person who would make a superstar want to register a marriage at home rather than rent out a Tuscan vineyard.

Aamir introduced her to the world in 2025, on his 60th birthday — a soft launch so understated it almost dared the press not to notice. They noticed. They have not stopped noticing since.

And that, more than the wedding itself, is what visibly irritates the man. Pressed on the media frenzy, Aamir let the mask of the unflappable perfectionist slip just slightly.

> "I don't see why there's all the frenzy. There is too much interest in the lives of celebrities, especially cricketers and actors. People should be interested in our work, not our personal lives. I don't know how the information on my wedding had leaked. These days, nothing is off bounds." — Aamir Khan


![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)


It's a familiar Aamir paradox: the most calculated star in the industry, the one who plans release strategies like military campaigns, genuinely baffled that anyone wants to know who he loves. Fans, meanwhile, have already migrated to Gauri's sparse Instagram, leaving "happy married life" under a photo of the two of them holding hands — congratulating a wedding that hasn't happened, on the account of a woman who clearly never asked for the spotlight.

The industry, predictably, has been warmer than the tabloids. At the recent celebration marking **25 years of Lagaan** and the silver jubilee of Aamir Khan Productions, **Kajol** stole the night with a line aimed straight at the groom — praising his production house for its "great taste in movies," then adding, to a roomful of laughter, that he also had "great taste in women." Aamir, sharing the stage with former wife **Kiran Rao** and co-stars Kajol and **Juhi Chawla**, looked visibly embarrassed — the rare sight of Mr. Perfectionist with nowhere to hide. Veteran actress **Rakhee Gulzar** had earlier defended his decision to marry again at 60, calling him "a very sincere person." When the old guard is this protective, you know the affection is real.

What makes this a diaspora story isn't the guest list — it's the template. For NRIs raised on the spectacle of the **Ambani-grade** Bollywood wedding, where the celebration is the content, Aamir doing the opposite is its own kind of statement. He has been married before. He has done the long, public marriages and the dignified, public separations. He maintains a famously cordial relationship with Reena Dutta, the mother of his children **Ira** and **Junaid Khan**, and with Kiran Rao. A man who has navigated three families across four decades isn't trying to prove anything with a fourth wedding. He's just done.

There will be no live stream, no exclusive magazine spread, no choreographed first dance for the diaspora to dissect over chai on Sunday morning. By the time most of us read about July 5, it'll already be over — a signature on a document, a few close friends, a Bengaluru wellness entrepreneur and a 61-year-old superstar deciding that the most radical thing a Khan can do in 2026 is keep something for himself.

Whether his closest friends — the other two Khans among them — actually show up remains the one detail he won't confirm. Some things, even Aamir Khan gets to keep private. For once, he's earned it.
